#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolve the origin GitHub repository and check a /sc:issue claim argument.

Standard library only. Wave 0 of both /sc:issue modes runs this script, so the
repository rule of the design (section 13) is tested code, not prose.

Usage:
    origin_repo.py
        Print ``owner/repo`` parsed from ``git remote get-url origin``.
    origin_repo.py --claim <number|#number|url>
        Resolve origin as above, then check the claim argument against it and
        print ``{"repo": "owner/repo", "number": N}`` as one JSON line.

Only the ``origin`` remote is read. ``gh repo set-default``, gh's fork-parent
default and every other remote are never consulted.

Accepted origin URLs (a trailing ``/`` is tolerated):
    https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
    https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
    git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>
    git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git

Claim argument rules (``check_claim``):
    ``302`` or ``#302``                         -> N = 302
    ``https://github.com/<origin>/issues/302``  -> N = 302; a trailing ``/``,
                                                   a ``#fragment`` or a
                                                   ``?query`` is ignored
    a GitHub URL naming any other owner or      -> E-FOREIGN-REPO
    repo, or naming no repo                        (owner and repo compare
                                                   case-insensitively and as
                                                   whole path segments, so
                                                   ``IronClaudeX`` is foreign)
    a URL (``<scheme>://...`` or               -> E-FOREIGN-REPO
    ``git@<host>:...``) on any host other
    than github.com
    ``https://github.com/<origin>/pull/302``    -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
    a GitHub URL on origin whose path is not    -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
    ``/issues/<N>``
    anything else (not a number, not a URL)     -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
A GitHub URL may start with ``https://``, ``http://`` or no scheme, may carry
``www.``, and may be written ``git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>/...``; every form
is read by the same rules above. N is read only from the path segment right
after ``/issues/``; digits in the owner or repo name never become N.

Exit codes and messages (the message goes to stderr):
    0  success
    1  E-NO-ORIGIN     no origin remote, git failed, or origin is not GitHub
    2  bad command-line arguments (argparse)
    3  E-FOREIGN-REPO  the claim URL names a repository other than origin
    4  E-NOT-AN-ISSUE  the claim argument is not an issue number or issue URL
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

EXIT_NO_ORIGIN = 1
EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO = 3
EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE = 4

_NAME = r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"
_ORIGIN_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(rf"^https://github\.com/(?P<owner>{_NAME})/(?P<repo>{_NAME})/?$"),
    re.compile(rf"^git@github\.com:(?P<owner>{_NAME})/(?P<repo>{_NAME})/?$"),
)
_GITHUB_URL = re.compile(
    r"^(?:(?:https?://)?(?:www\.)?github\.com/|git@github\.com:)(?P<path>[^?#]*)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^#?(?P<n>[1-9][0-9]*)$")


class ClaimError(Exception):
    """A claim argument that /sc:issue must STOP on."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, exit_code: int, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.exit_code = exit_code


def parse_origin_url(url: str) -> str | None:
    """Return ``owner/repo`` for a GitHub origin URL, else ``None``."""
    url = url.strip()
    for pattern in _ORIGIN_PATTERNS:
        match = pattern.match(url)
        if match:
            owner = match.group("owner")
            repo = match.group("repo")
            if repo.endswith(".git"):
                repo = repo[: -len(".git")]
            if not repo or owner in (".", "..") or repo in (".", ".."):
                return None
            return "/".join((owner, repo))
    return None


def check_claim(arg: str, origin: str) -> int:
    """Return the issue number a claim argument names on ``origin``.

    Raises ``ClaimError`` with ``E-FOREIGN-REPO`` or ``E-NOT-AN-ISSUE``.
    """
    arg = arg.strip()
    number = _NUMBER.match(arg)
    if number:
        return int(number.group("n"))

    url = _GITHUB_URL.match(arg)
    if not url:
        if "://" in arg or arg.lower().startswith("git@"):
            raise ClaimError(
                "E-FOREIGN-REPO",
                EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO,
                f"{arg} is not a GitHub URL, so it is not on the origin repo {origin}",
            )
        raise ClaimError(
            "E-NOT-AN-ISSUE",
            EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE,
            f"{arg} is not an issue number or an issue URL",
        )

    segments = [s for s in url.group("path").split("/") if s]
    if len(segments) < 2:
        raise ClaimError(
            "E-FOREIGN-REPO", EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO, f"{arg} names no repository"
        )
    owner, repo = segments[0], segments[1]
    if repo.lower().endswith(".git"):
        repo = repo[: -len(".git")]
    origin_owner, origin_repo = origin.split("/", 1)
    if owner.lower() != origin_owner.lower() or repo.lower() != origin_repo.lower():
        raise ClaimError(
            "E-FOREIGN-REPO",
            EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO,
            "/".join((owner, repo)) + f" is not the origin repo {origin}",
        )

    rest = segments[2:]
    if len(rest) == 2 and rest[0] == "issues":
        number = _NUMBER.match(rest[1])
        if number and not rest[1].startswith("#"):
            return int(number.group("n"))
    if rest and rest[0] == "pull":
        raise ClaimError(
            "E-NOT-AN-ISSUE",
            EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE,
            f"{arg} is a pull request, not an issue",
        )
    raise ClaimError("E-NOT-AN-ISSUE", EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE, f"{arg} is not an issue URL")


def read_origin() -> str:
    """Return ``owner/repo`` of the ``origin`` remote, or raise ``ClaimError``."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    except OSError as exc:
        raise ClaimError(
            "E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, f"git could not run: {exc}"
        ) from exc
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ClaimError("E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, "no origin remote")
    parsed = parse_origin_url(result.stdout)
    if parsed is None:
        raise ClaimError("E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, "origin is not a GitHub URL")
    return parsed


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--claim", metavar="NUMBER_OR_URL")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        origin = read_origin()
        if args.claim is None:
            print(origin)
            return 0
        number = check_claim(args.claim, origin)
    except ClaimError as exc:
        print(f"{exc.code}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return exc.exit_code
    print(json.dumps({"repo": origin, "number": number}))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Resolve the origin GitHub repository and check a /sc:issue claim argument.
3	
4	Standard library only. Wave 0 of both /sc:issue modes runs this script, so the
5	repository rule of the design (section 13) is tested code, not prose.
6	
7	Usage:
8	    origin_repo.py
9	        Print ``owner/repo`` parsed from ``git remote get-url origin``.
10	    origin_repo.py --claim <number|#number|url>
11	        Resolve origin as above, then check the claim argument against it and
12	        print ``{"repo": "owner/repo", "number": N}`` as one JSON line.
13	
14	Only the ``origin`` remote is read. ``gh repo set-default``, gh's fork-parent
15	default and every other remote are never consulted.
16	
17	Accepted origin URLs (a trailing ``/`` is tolerated):
18	    https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>
19	    https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
20	    git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>
21	    git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git
22	
23	Claim argument rules (``check_claim``):
24	    ``302`` or ``#302``                         -> N = 302
25	    ``https://github.com/<origin>/issues/302``  -> N = 302; a trailing ``/``,
26	                                                   a ``#fragment`` or a
27	                                                   ``?query`` is ignored
28	    a GitHub URL naming any other owner or      -> E-FOREIGN-REPO
29	    repo, or naming no repo                        (owner and repo compare
30	                                                   case-insensitively and as
31	                                                   whole path segments, so
32	                                                   ``IronClaudeX`` is foreign)
33	    a URL (``<scheme>://...`` or               -> E-FOREIGN-REPO
34	    ``git@<host>:...``) on any host other
35	    than github.com
36	    ``https://github.com/<origin>/pull/302``    -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
37	    a GitHub URL on origin whose path is not    -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
38	    ``/issues/<N>``
39	    anything else (not a number, not a URL)     -> E-NOT-AN-ISSUE
40	A GitHub URL may start with ``https://``, ``http://`` or no scheme, may carry
41	``www.``, and may be written ``git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>/...``; every form
42	is read by the same rules above. N is read only from the path segment right
43	after ``/issues/``; digits in the owner or repo name never become N.
44	
45	Exit codes and messages (the message goes to stderr):
46	    0  success
47	    1  E-NO-ORIGIN     no origin remote, git failed, or origin is not GitHub
48	    2  bad command-line arguments (argparse)
49	    3  E-FOREIGN-REPO  the claim URL names a repository other than origin
50	    4  E-NOT-AN-ISSUE  the claim argument is not an issue number or issue URL
51	"""
52	
53	from __future__ import annotations
54	
55	import argparse
56	import json
57	import re
58	import subprocess
59	import sys
60	
61	EXIT_NO_ORIGIN = 1
62	EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO = 3
63	EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE = 4
64	
65	_NAME = r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"
66	_ORIGIN_PATTERNS = (
67	    re.compile(rf"^https://github\.com/(?P<owner>{_NAME})/(?P<repo>{_NAME})/?$"),
68	    re.compile(rf"^git@github\.com:(?P<owner>{_NAME})/(?P<repo>{_NAME})/?$"),
69	)
70	_GITHUB_URL = re.compile(
71	    r"^(?:(?:https?://)?(?:www\.)?github\.com/|git@github\.com:)(?P<path>[^?#]*)",
72	    re.IGNORECASE,
73	)
74	_NUMBER = re.compile(r"^#?(?P<n>[1-9][0-9]*)$")
75	
76	
77	class ClaimError(Exception):
78	    """A claim argument that /sc:issue must STOP on."""
79	
80	    def __init__(self, code: str, exit_code: int, message: str) -> None:
81	        super().__init__(message)
82	        self.code = code
83	        self.exit_code = exit_code
84	
85	
86	def parse_origin_url(url: str) -> str | None:
87	    """Return ``owner/repo`` for a GitHub origin URL, else ``None``."""
88	    url = url.strip()
89	    for pattern in _ORIGIN_PATTERNS:
90	        match = pattern.match(url)
91	        if match:
92	            owner = match.group("owner")
93	            repo = match.group("repo")
94	            if repo.endswith(".git"):
95	                repo = repo[: -len(".git")]
96	            if not repo or owner in (".", "..") or repo in (".", ".."):
97	                return None
98	            return "/".join((owner, repo))
99	    return None
100	
101	
102	def check_claim(arg: str, origin: str) -> int:
103	    """Return the issue number a claim argument names on ``origin``.
104	
105	    Raises ``ClaimError`` with ``E-FOREIGN-REPO`` or ``E-NOT-AN-ISSUE``.
106	    """
107	    arg = arg.strip()
108	    number = _NUMBER.match(arg)
109	    if number:
110	        return int(number.group("n"))
111	
112	    url = _GITHUB_URL.match(arg)
113	    if not url:
114	        if "://" in arg or arg.lower().startswith("git@"):
115	            raise ClaimError(
116	                "E-FOREIGN-REPO",
117	                EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO,
118	                f"{arg} is not a GitHub URL, so it is not on the origin repo {origin}",
119	            )
120	        raise ClaimError(
121	            "E-NOT-AN-ISSUE",
122	            EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE,
123	            f"{arg} is not an issue number or an issue URL",
124	        )
125	
126	    segments = [s for s in url.group("path").split("/") if s]
127	    if len(segments) < 2:
128	        raise ClaimError(
129	            "E-FOREIGN-REPO", EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO, f"{arg} names no repository"
130	        )
131	    owner, repo = segments[0], segments[1]
132	    if repo.lower().endswith(".git"):
133	        repo = repo[: -len(".git")]
134	    origin_owner, origin_repo = origin.split("/", 1)
135	    if owner.lower() != origin_owner.lower() or repo.lower() != origin_repo.lower():
136	        raise ClaimError(
137	            "E-FOREIGN-REPO",
138	            EXIT_FOREIGN_REPO,
139	            "/".join((owner, repo)) + f" is not the origin repo {origin}",
140	        )
141	
142	    rest = segments[2:]
143	    if len(rest) == 2 and rest[0] == "issues":
144	        number = _NUMBER.match(rest[1])
145	        if number and not rest[1].startswith("#"):
146	            return int(number.group("n"))
147	    if rest and rest[0] == "pull":
148	        raise ClaimError(
149	            "E-NOT-AN-ISSUE",
150	            EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE,
151	            f"{arg} is a pull request, not an issue",
152	        )
153	    raise ClaimError("E-NOT-AN-ISSUE", EXIT_NOT_AN_ISSUE, f"{arg} is not an issue URL")
154	
155	
156	def read_origin() -> str:
157	    """Return ``owner/repo`` of the ``origin`` remote, or raise ``ClaimError``."""
158	    try:
159	        result = subprocess.run(
160	            ["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"],
161	            capture_output=True,
162	            text=True,
163	            check=False,
164	        )
165	    except OSError as exc:
166	        raise ClaimError(
167	            "E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, f"git could not run: {exc}"
168	        ) from exc
169	    if result.returncode != 0:
170	        raise ClaimError("E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, "no origin remote")
171	    parsed = parse_origin_url(result.stdout)
172	    if parsed is None:
173	        raise ClaimError("E-NO-ORIGIN", EXIT_NO_ORIGIN, "origin is not a GitHub URL")
174	    return parsed
175	
176	
177	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
178	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
179	    parser.add_argument("--claim", metavar="NUMBER_OR_URL")
180	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
181	    try:
182	        origin = read_origin()
183	        if args.claim is None:
184	            print(origin)
185	            return 0
186	        number = check_claim(args.claim, origin)
187	    except ClaimError as exc:
188	        print(f"{exc.code}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
189	        return exc.exit_code
190	    print(json.dumps({"repo": origin, "number": number}))
191	    return 0
192	
193	
194	if __name__ == "__main__":
195	    sys.exit(main())

25	Explicit only: the user types `/sc:issue --claim ...` or `/sc:issue --create ...`.
26	
27	## Usage
28	
29	```text
30	/sc:issue --claim <number|url> [--pipeline worktree|full|none] [--submit]
31	/sc:issue --create "<description>" [--depth quick|standard|deep] [--mode feature|bug] [--type <type>]
32	```
33	
34	## Options
35	
36	| Flag | Mode | Default | Values | Meaning |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| `--claim` | claim | - | issue number (`302`, `#302`) or issue URL on the origin repo | Claim this issue |
39	| `--create` | create | - | free text, or `@path` to a file holding the description | Description of the feature or bug |
40	| `--depth` | create | `quick` | `quick`, `standard`, `deep` | How hard the command checks the flags and fills the body |
41	| `--mode` | create | chosen by a worker when omitted | `feature`, `bug` | Picks the feature or bug template, the Feature or Bug issue type and the `enhancement` / `bug` label |
42	| `--type` | create | chosen by a worker when omitted | `cicd`, `command`, `skill`, `agent`, `hook`, `cli`, `core`, `docs`, `tests`, `install`, `other` | Area of the change; a feature in `tests` gets the issue type Test, otherwise the area is recorded in `flags.md`; no label is applied for it |
43	| `--pipeline` | claim | `full` or `worktree`, picked from the issue | `worktree`, `full`, `none` | How far the launched agent goes. Omitted means the level is picked from the issue: a bug or a simple or medium feature of 16 hours or less gets `full`; a complex feature, a feature over 16 hours or an issue that cannot be classified gets `worktree` (the rule is in the skill, `refs/claim.md`). `worktree` and `full` create the worktree and launch an agent; `none` creates no worktree and launches no agent |
44	| `--submit` | claim | off | no value | Only with `--pipeline full` (an explicit `--pipeline full` is still required): the agent also commits, pushes a feature branch to `origin` and runs `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`. Never merges |
45	| `--stage` | claim | none (the recommended chain) | `research`, `spec`, `plan`, `debug` | The Project Status the issue is in; the issue watcher sends it. Step 1 of the next steps becomes that stage's command, and the claim skips `/sc:recommend` (`recommend.md` says so; without `--stage` the claim still runs it) (`/sc:research`, `/sc:design` or `/sc:brainstorm`, `/sc:workflow`, `/sc:troubleshoot`; `--fix` only with `--pipeline full`). Valid with every `--pipeline` value; the launched agent's last step is writing `.dev/issues/<N>/result.md` |
46	
47	There is no repository option (the repo is always `origin`), no dry-run option and no preview option.
48	
49	A person who types `--claim` with no `--pipeline` gets the picked level, and an explicit `--pipeline` always wins. The issue watcher never relies on the default: it always passes `--pipeline none`. `--submit` still needs an explicit `--pipeline full`.
50	
51	## STOP rules (checked before Activation)
52	
53	- Exactly one of `--claim` / `--create` is required. Both or neither: STOP and print the Usage block.
54	- `--depth`, `--mode` or `--type` together with `--claim`: STOP `E-CREATE-ONLY-FLAG` ("--depth, --mode and --type apply to --create only").
55	- An unknown value for `--depth`, `--mode` or `--type`: STOP and list the allowed values from the Options table.
56	- An empty `--create` description (or an `@path` file that is empty or missing): STOP ("--create needs a description").
57	- An empty `--claim` argument: STOP and print the Usage block.
58	- `--pipeline` or `--submit` together with `--create`: STOP `E-CLAIM-ONLY-FLAG` ("--pipeline and --submit apply to --claim only").
59	- A `--pipeline` value that is not `worktree`, `full` or `none`, or `--pipeline` with no value: STOP and list those three values.
60	- `--submit` with a value, without `--pipeline full`, or with no `--pipeline`: STOP `E-SUBMIT-NEEDS-FULL` ("--submit needs --pipeline full").
61	- `--stage` together with `--create`: STOP `E-CLAIM-ONLY-FLAG` ("--stage applies to --claim only").
62	- A `--stage` value that is not `research`, `spec`, `plan` or `debug`, or `--stage` with no value: STOP and list those four values.
63	
64	## Examples
65	
66	```text
67	/sc:issue --claim 302
68	/sc:issue --claim https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/302
69	/sc:issue --claim 302 --pipeline worktree
70	/sc:issue --claim 302 --pipeline none
71	/sc:issue --claim 302 --pipeline full
72	/sc:issue --claim 302 --pipeline full --submit
73	/sc:issue --claim 302 --pipeline worktree --stage plan
74	/sc:issue --create "The sync check misses deleted skill files" --mode bug --type cli --depth standard
75	/sc:issue --create @notes/new-command.md --depth deep
76	```
77	
78	## Outputs
79	
80	Every file starts from a template of the skill and stays under `.dev/issues/`:
81	
82	| Mode | Directory | Files |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| claim | `.dev/issues/<N>/` | `scout.md`, `clickup.json`, `accuracy-check.md` (posted), `issue-summary.md` (effort in hours), `analysis/analyze-<scope>.md` (only when the issue is out of date), `recommend.md`, `next-steps.md`, `launch-prompt.md` (the launched agent's instructions; not written for `--pipeline none`), `claim-comment.md` (posted), `worktree.json` (the worktree path and launch record; never copied into the worktree; not written for `--pipeline none`), `launch-result.json` (the full launch JSON of a launched or failed launch; never copied into the worktree; not written for `--pipeline none`) |
85	| create | `.dev/issues/draft-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<slug>/`, renamed to `.dev/issues/<N>/` once the issue exists | `description.md`, `scout.md`, `flags.md`, `issue-body.md` (posted), `draft-notes.md` (added material and assumptions are kept there, in the body, and printed in the final output), and `create-review.md` (posted only when a standard or deep check disagrees with your flags) |
86	
87	After a claim, the launched agent works from `.dev/issues/<N>/launch-prompt.md` and `next-steps.md` in the worktree, in order, after the `/model` line `next-steps.md` starts with. With `--pipeline none` no worktree is created and no agent is launched: open `.dev/issues/<N>/next-steps.md` in this checkout and run its commands in your own session.
88	
89	Coordinator handoff for `--pipeline none`: the claim leaves its files in the checkout that ran it. When a coordinator owns the issue, it runs the `worktree` step of `orca_worktree.py` (the repository, the issue number, the base branch and that folder as its arguments) and then `worker-start --worktree path:<the printed path>`. The script creates the worktree with no agent, because it must copy `.dev/issues/<N>/` into the worktree before any agent starts (a create that carries an agent would start that agent before the copy), and it closes the plain first tab Orca opens, so the coordinator must run `worker-start` straight after it, which supplies the agent. If the coordinator is down or stops between the script and `worker-start`, the worktree stays empty, with no agent and no terminal, and nothing runs in it. On its next wake the coordinator finds its adoption row still `reserved`: a start may or may not have happened, so it never starts again by itself. It reads `worker-list`; a worker in that worktree settles the row as `started` with its Dispatch id, and with no worker the row stays for a person to settle. A later worktree step for the same issue reuses the existing worktree through the script's reuse lookup (marker, record, basename, branch) instead of creating a second `issue-<N>`. A person sees such a worktree in `orca worktree ps` with an empty `agents` list and can start the coordinator or remove the worktree with `orca worktree rm`.
